Middle East.headline: Gaza’s displaced face a deadly choice: collapsing buildings or flooded tents
Middle East.body: With thousands of buildings damaged and the punishing winter fast approaching, displaced Palestinians sheltering inside Gaza’s ruins face two bitter choices: sleep beneath unstable concrete or risk having nowhere to stay at all. Pieces of concrete sometimes break loose without warning, and stones tumble from damaged walls. Yet fear of the coming winter drives families to seek any shelter with a concrete roof, no matter how fractured it may be. They view these broken structures as their final line of defence against the looming winter storms. However, this choice carries potentially catastrophic risks. Middle East.headline: Pennsylvania announces sixth death in measles outbreak as case numbers rise
Middle East.body: Latest fatality is unvaccinated woman, 39, with ‘underlying conditions’ but CDC still lists only two deaths nationwide A sixth death has been announced in Pennsylvania ’s measles outbreak, as new figures show cases in the state have risen above 1,100. The most recent fatality was reported in Franklin county on Monday in a statement posted to Facebook by its coroner. The victim was identified as a 39-year-old female who “had several underlying conditions, including a past diagnosis of measles with treatment”. Continue reading...

Americas.headline: Two deaths reported as Hurricane Simon, storm Rachel batter Mexico’s coast
Americas.body: At least two people have died in Mexico after Hurricane Simon and former tropical storm Rachel brought torrential rain and catastrophic flooding to Pacific coast communities. At a Monday news briefing, Guerrero Governor Evelyn Salgado confirmed that a 71-year-old man had died during Hurricane Simon after a retaining wall collapsed under the weight of intense precipitation. Americas.headline: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five people on Mexico’s Pacific coast
Americas.body: Security forces use helicopters to rescue dozens of people as the two storms damage infrastructure and cause flash flooding At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel pummelled Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes. Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man who died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo in the southern state of Guerrero, governor Evelyn Salgado said at a press conference. Continue reading...

Africa.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Rapidly expanding Ebola outbreak
Africa.body: The United Nations warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is growing exponentially and risks spreading into neighboring countries. According to the UN senior Ebola coordinator, the epidemic covers an area larger than France, with half of all recorded fatalities occurring within a recent 20-day window. Containment operations are failing to outpace transmission rates, prompting urgent calls for additional humanitarian funding and the rapid dispatch of aid resources to remote regions.

Africa.headline: Sudan — Airstrike kills 72 near border amid rising drone attacks
Africa.body: Sudan's military leadership ordered an investigation into a airstrike on a gold mining site in the Jabal al-Uqaydat area near the Egyptian border that killed 72 people. A local rights group accused Egyptian forces of conducting the raid, though the claim remains unverified and Egypt has not commented. Separately, reports indicate drone strikes targeted a displacement site in Blue Nile State, causing casualties primarily among women and children amid escalating nationwide violence.

Africa.headline: Somalia — Escalating conflict in Baidoa heightens humanitarian risks
Africa.body: The United Nations resident and humanitarian coordinator for Somalia appealed for an immediate cessation of hostilities in Baidoa, warning that fighting in the South West State capital is worsening severe humanitarian distress. The clashes severely impact displaced communities, women, children, older persons, and people with disabilities. UN officials called on all armed factions to safeguard civilians and public infrastructure while facilitating unhindered access for relief organizations operating amid severe drought, flood risks, and food insecurity.

Europe.headline: IMF global economic forecast shows 'resilience under strain'
Europe.body: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts that global economic output will slow to 3.1% this year in spite of geopolitical disruptions, but warns that high inflation and AI share valuations could be risks for financial stability. Also in this edition: Russia says it has exported $320 billion worth of oil and gas to European countries since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, despite sanctions. Plus: Dangote refinery extends its IPO deadline by two weeks to attract even more retail investors.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar military airstrikes on Rakhine displacement camps kill eight, rebel group says
Asia-Pacific.body: Myanmar military airstrikes on camps for internally displaced people in Rakhine State have killed eight people over two days, a rebel group and a youth association said today (5 September), a week after an aerial attack in the same state killed 50. - On Sunday, an airstrike hit a camp for internally displaced people in Rakhine's Ponnagyun township at around 5 p.m. (1030 GMT), killing six people and injuring 11 others, according to spokespersons for the Arakan Army and the Ponnagyun Youth Association - On Monday morning, both groups said another airstrike hit a second camp in the same township, killing two people and injuring two others - "Everyone there is a displaced civilian," said Kyaw Wi

Asia-Pacific.headline: Indonesia wildfire fuelled by El Niño razes almost 300 homes
Asia-Pacific.body: Hundreds of people displaced in Bangka Belitung province as shift in wind direction drove blaze towards settlement A forest fire on Indonesia’s Sumatra island fuelled by El Niño has razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official said on Tuesday as the country battles devastating blazes and haze. Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitung province on Saturday and tried to put it out themselves with portable water pumps, said the head of South Bangka regency, Riza Herdavid. Continue reading...

Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: How a Gravedigger Became a Hero: King Solomon and the 1833 Cholera Epidemic - Our Ameri...
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: On this episode of Our American Stories, in the summer of 1833, Lexington, Kentucky, was brought to its knees by a cholera outbreak. Entire families were lost in a matter of days, and fear spread faster than the disease itself. When the dead outnumbered the living willing to bury them, one man stepped forward. His name was Solomon. Most people in town dismissed him as a drunk gravedigger. But in the middle of the crisis, he dug without stopping, gave the dead their dignity, and kept the city from collapsing under the weight of its own fear.
